claim.pdf_says: and each corresponding occurrence of the data item referenced by identifier-2.
claim.markdown_says: and each corresponding occurrence of the data item referenced by identifier-**2**.
claim.why_it_matters: Stray markdown emphasis delimiters were injected around the operand ordinal; the PDF prints plain 'identifier-2'. Read as plain text (how the spec is grepped for operand names) the token becomes 'identifier-**2**', so a literal search for 'identifier-2' misses this sentence. Known recurring artifact - the same pattern appears at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 32469 ('literal-**1**', 'identifier-**2**', 'character positions**.**') - so it should be swept, not fixed in isolation.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED against the rendered page. Rendered specs page 545 at 300dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v545/spec_p545.png) and cropped the final line of General rule 8 at 1.3x. The printed glyphs read: 'and each corresponding occurrence of the data item referenced by identifier-2.' The token 'identifier-2' is set in the same upright roman face and the same stroke weight as every surrounding word - the '2' is NOT bold, NOT italic, and carries no distinguishing styling whatsoever. There is no emphasis anywhere in the sentence. The canonical markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 22821 (workunit md_source_line 22814, page-545 anchor) reads '...referenced by identifier-**2**.' - verified byte-exact via `sed -n '22821p' | cat -A`, so both sides of the claim are quoted accurately. Adversarial checks, all of which FAILED to refute: (1) Not reflow or line-wrap - the entire sentence sits on one markdown line and the emphasis markers are interior to a single token, not an artifact of joining lines. (2) Not hyphenation - the only hyphen is the legitimate one in 'identifier-2', which is present in both sources. (3) Not page-break furniture - the sentence is wholly contained on page 545 in both sources. (4) Not a faithful rendering of PDF styling - this is the key test, and the crop settles it: there is nothing bold on the page for the '**' to represent. The transcription injected four characters that do not exist in the source. (5) Not benign-when-rendered - `identifier-**2**` renders as identifier-2, i.e. a spuriously bold digit, so the defect is visible in the rendered view too, not merely in raw text. The difference does not change the SEMANTICS of the rule (a human still reads 'identifier-2'), which is why 'cosmetic' is the right severity; but it is a genuine content discrepancy - characters present in the transcription and absent from the source, injected mid-token - and it defeats the grep-by-operand-name workflow the spec is actually used through. The claim's cross-reference is also correct: line 32469 reads verbatim '...specified by either literal-**1** or the value of the data item referenced by identifier-**2**...' and ends '...number of character positions**.**', confirming both the operand-ordinal variant and a punctuation variant of the same artifact.
verdict.corrected_description: Claim is REAL and accurately quoted; only its scope was understated. Page 545 / specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 22821: the transcription emits 'identifier-**2**' where the PDF prints plain, unstyled 'identifier-2' (verified glyph-by-glyph on a 300dpi render - no bold, no italic, no emphasis anywhere in General rule 8). The stray-emphasis artifact is systematic, not a one-off pair: a sweep of the whole transcription finds 50 occurrences of the operand-ordinal form <operand>-**<digit>** across 29 lines, clustering in four contiguous runs at md pages 346 (lines 14956-14978: file-name, data-name, literal, integer), 418 (lines 17949-17967: integer-1 / integer-2, ~15 occurrences), 545 (this instance, isolated), and 801 (lines 32465-32475: identifier-1/2/4/5/7, literal-1). A related punctuation variant - emphasis wrapped around a trailing period, e.g. 'character positions**.**' - occurs 3 times, one of them on line 32469. Recommended remediation is a single mechanical sweep removing the injected '**' pairs across all 29 lines plus the 3 punctuation cases, rather than an isolated edit to line 22821. Note that only the page-545 instance was visually verified against the PDF here; the other three clusters are pattern matches on the markdown and should be spot-checked against their own renders before the sweep lands.
